items.title: If the categories of dotted arrows are setoids then the diagonal is separated

items.difficulty_reason: The counted statement shows that a morphism of algebraic stacks has separated diagonal as soon as its diagonal is quasi-separated and the categories of dotted arrows in the valuative diagrams of the relevant definition are setoids (author lemma at source lines 9450-9458, label lemma-setoids-and-diagonal). The proof (source lines 9460-9528) reduces to the universal closedness of the second diagonal through the inertia, proves the existence part of the valuative criterion by unwinding the 2-categorical definitions until the setoid hypothesis forces the difference of two automorphisms to be the identity, and then transports the criterion along a smooth base change to a quasi-compact morphism of algebraic spaces, where it implies universal closedness (proof lines 9466-9527). The 2-categorical unwinding in the existence part is the content. H3.
